claims.text: The grants cover tuition fees for undergraduate students.
The grants are for students from low-income households.
The grants are for students ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government.
The grants are for students studying at eligible Scottish higher education institutions.
The grants cover up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
Applications are open from June 1, 2026, to December 1, 2026.
The application portal will be open for grants covering the academic year 2026-27.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applications will be processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
Applicants must have an unconditional offer for, or be a continuing student on, an undergraduate degree course at specific Scottish institutions or a course validated by these institutions.
HNC and HND diploma courses are not eligible for support.
Access courses are not eligible for support.
Accelerated degree courses with a graduate entry are not eligible for support.
Courses delivered by, or at, a university outside Scotland are not eligible for support.
Courses at a Scottish Higher Education Institute delivered and validated by a university outside Scotland are not eligible for support.
Open University courses are not eligible for support.
Continuing Professional Development (CPD) courses are not eligible for support.
University courses below degree level, e.g. Diploma or Certificate courses, are not eligible for support.
Postgraduate degrees are not eligible for support.

The Carnegie Education Fund has a budget to fund students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start an undergraduate degree in a different field of study in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must enter the first year of their course in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must have been unable to gain employment in the subject area of their previous degree, be unemployed, have been made redundant or are facing redundancy.

Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must wish to reskill in a different field of study, unrelated to their previous qualifications and recognised as being in a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.
The grants are for students who do not have the financial resources to attend university.
The median household income of award-holders in 2025-26 was £10,000 per year.
All applications are made online.
Applicants must complete an eligibility checker before applying.
An automatic reply confirms receipt of a submitted complete application.
Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted unless the student was first informed that SAAS would not be covering their fees after the online portal closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome within two to three weeks, provided all requested information and a timely referee response are submitted.
Applicants must provide evidence of their eligibility.
Applicants must provide a letter of acceptance for their university course or evidence of enrollment if a returning student.
Applicants must provide their SAAS Award Notice letter showing ineligibility for tuition fee support and the amount of maintenance loan awarded.

Applicants must provide a P60 for the tax year ending April 2026, or pay slips or Universal Credit statements covering the last 3 months for the applicant (if 25 or over) and their spouse/partner, or for the applicant and their parent(s)/guardian(s) (if under 25).
Students receiving a SAAS bursary must also provide a copy of their SAAS award letter.
Supporting evidence can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images.
There is a 5MB size limit on each file submitted online.
